# RS3 Clientscript


### VM design
The cs2 VM is a stack machine which uses supports three primitive types (int,long,string). All types can be represtend by one of those three. The VM keeps a seperate stack for each of these primitives.

#### The stacks
- There are tree stacks (int,long,string).
- You can only access to last pushed value per stack
- However the VM does not enforce ordered access so eg: pushint->pushstring->popint->popstring would be valid
  - The Jagex cs2 compiler generally avoids this, but it can happen for script calls
- The total stack size for each stack is limited to 1000 entries
- There seems to be no hardcoded string length limit


#### Scripts calls
- Functions get their own set of local variables (similar to registers), the number of vars is declared in the script metadata
- When a script is called its arguments will be popped from stack and placed in the corresponding local variable slots.
- Callees do not get an isolated stack. It is possible (but highly discouraged) to pop values from stack that weren't defined as script argument.
- The stack is not used to store local variables when calling another script.
  - presumably this means that there is a seperate recursion limit caused by some sort of "local variable stack"


#### Branching
- The max script length seems to be 65535 ops. After that weird stuff starts happening
- All jumps are relative. (relative to index + 1)
- When none of the switch branches match the VM will simply go to the next instruction
- Switch statements can only jump forward
- All other branching ops can go back and forward

#### Arrays
- Arrays are weird

1	# Map renderer
2	The part of the source is used to render the world map used on RuneApps.org. 
3	
4	## Simple setup
5	
6	Copy the mapconfig.jsonc file below to a new folder called extract_map, then run the following shell code
7	```sh
8	npm run nodegl -- dist/maprender -o openrs2:1720 -c extract_map/mapconfig.jsonc
9	# the nodegl script opens an electron window and runs the nodejs command in it
10	#  dist/maprender -> the map render script
11	#  -o openrs2:1720 -> use cache id 1720 from openrs2.org as cache source
12	#  -c extract_map/mapconfig.jsonc -> use the config file at the given location
13	```
14	
15	### Example config
16	```jsonc
17	//extract_map/mapconfig.jsonc
18	{
19	    "$schema": "../generated/maprenderconfig.schema.json",
20	    //test gives a 3x3 area around lumby, "main" for the main world map, "full" for everything, a list of rectangles is also accepted eg: "50.50,20.20-70.70"
21	    "area": "test",
22	    //the size of the output images, usually 256 or 512
23	    "tileimgsize": 512,
24	    //set to true to keep the output y origin at the bottom left, equal to the game z origin

# Map renderer
The part of the source is used to render the world map used on RuneApps.org. 

## Simple setup

Copy the mapconfig.jsonc file below to a new folder called extract_map, then run the following shell code
```sh
npm run nodegl -- dist/maprender -o openrs2:1720 -c extract_map/mapconfig.jsonc
# the nodegl script opens an electron window and runs the nodejs command in it
#  dist/maprender -> the map render script
#  -o openrs2:1720 -> use cache id 1720 from openrs2.org as cache source
#  -c extract_map/mapconfig.jsonc -> use the config file at the given location
```

### Example config
```jsonc
//extract_map/mapconfig.jsonc
{
    "$schema": "../generated/maprenderconfig.schema.json",
    //test gives a 3x3 area around lumby, "main" for the main world map, "full" for everything, a list of rectangles is also accepted eg: "50.50,20.20-70.70"
    "area": "test",
    //the size of the output images, usually 256 or 512
    "tileimgsize": 512,
    //set to true to keep the output y origin at the bottom left, equal to the game z origin
    "noyflip": false,
    //set to true to keep output chunks aligned with in-game chunks. Incurs performance penalty as more neighbouring chunks have to be loaded
    "nochunkoffset": false,
    //list of layers to render
    "layers": [
        {
            "name": "3d", //name of the layer, this will be the folder name
            "mode": "3d", //3d world render
            "format": "webp", //currently only png and webp. jpeg in theory supported but not implemented or tested
            "level": 0, //floor level of the render, 0 means ground floor and all roofs are hidden, highest level is 3 which makes all roofs visible
            "pxpersquare": 64, //the level of detail for highest zoom level measured in pixels per map tile (1x1 meter). Subject to pxpersquare*64>tileimgsize, because it is currently not possible to render less than one image per mapchunk
            "dxdy": 0.15, //dxdy and dzdy to determine the view angle, 0,0 for straight down, something like 0.15,0.25 for birds eye
            "dzdy": 0.25
        },
        {
            "name": "map",
            "mode": "map", //old style 2d map render
            "format": "png",
            "level": 0,
            "pxpersquare": 64,
            "mapicons": true,
            "wallsonly": false //can be turned on to create a walls overlay layer to use on top of an existing 3d layer
        },
        {
            "name": "collision",
            "mode": "collision", //pathing/line of sight as overlay image layer to use on "map" or "3d"
            "format": "png",
            "level": 0,
            "pxpersquare": 64
        },
        {
            "name": "height",
            "mode": "height", //binary file per chunk containing 16bit height data and 16 bits of collision data in base3 per tile
            "level": 0,
            "pxpersquare": 1, //unused but required
            "usegzip": true //gzips the resulting file, need some server config to serve the compressed file
        },
        {
            "name": "locs",
            "mode": "locs", //json file with locs per chunk
            "level": 0,
            "pxpersquare": 1, //unused but required
            "usegzip": false
        },
        {
            "name": "maplabels",
            "mode": "maplabels", //json file per chunk containing maplabel images and uses
            "level": 0,
            "pxpersquare": 1,
            "usegzip": false
        },
        {
            "name": "rendermeta",
            "mode": "rendermeta", //advanced - json file containing metadata about the chunk render, used to dedupe historic renders
            "level": 0,
            "pxpersquare": 1
        },
        {
            "name": "interactions",
            "mode": "interactions", //json file per offset map chunk with loc info and images for all interactable locs
            "pxpersquare": 64, //same arguments as mode="3d"
            "dxdy": 0.15,
            "dzdy": 0.25,
            "format": "webp",
            "level": 0,
            "usegzip": true
        }
    ],
    //used to determine lowest scaling mip level, should generally always be 100,200 which ensures the lowest mip level contains the entire rs world in one image
    "mapsizex": 100,
    "mapsizez": 200
}

**You must NEVER use mocks, fakes, or stubbed data.**
- All code must run against REAL environments (Ollama, local SQLite, actual file systems).

- No `jest.fn()` or placeholder mocks allowed.

- Use the `YaoState` system to signal actual operational levels (Online, Degraded, Stressed).
- **Example**: Don't commit `function verify() { return true; // stub }`.

**Zero tolerance for type errors.**
- `npm run build` must succeed without warnings.
- Avoid `any` at all costs; use `unknown` with strict type guards.
- All public APIs must have explicit return types.

- No `console.log` in production engine code.

# 🧬 Sovereign Contributor Guide (POG2)

Welcome to the Sovereign Organism. Contributing to POG2 requires adherence to clinical standards, philosophical integrity, and a DOC-first mindset.

---

## 🚀 Sovereign Developer Must-Apply Checklist (DO NOT SKIP)

### 1. Neurological Mapping 🧬
Before writing code, identify where the new component fits in the `NeurologicalMap.ts`.
- **CNS**: High-level routing, strategy, and orchestration.
- **MEMORY**: Key-value stores, vector databases, context management.
- **SENSORY**: External probes, monitoring, vision, and shell interaction.
- **MOTOR**: Generative output, code application, and renderer operations.
- **REGISTRY**: All new limbs/engines must be registered in [NeurologicalMap.ts](src/state/NeurologicalMap.ts) AND added to the [CODEBASE_MAP.md](CODEBASE_MAP.md).

### 2. Clinical Planning 📝
Use the Kimi orchestrator to design the implementation.
- Create an `implementation_plan.md` in the brain.
- Define the `SovereignDomain` (CODE, SYSTEM, VISION, etc.).
- Ensure the decision path follows **Ternary Routing** (Yin/Yang/Yao).

### 3. Real Implementation (NO MOCKS) 🛠️
Implement the logic against real substrates.
- No stubbed APIs.
- Mandatory `Result<T>` pattern for all fallible calls.
- Strict type safety (Zero TSC errors).
- **Trauma-Informed Logic**: Follow safety rules (Circuit Breaker, Reasoning Traces) in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md#%F0%9F%9B%A1%EF%B8%8F-trauma-informed-development-rules).

### 4. Neurological Auditing 🔬
Every new node MUST be auditable.
- Add a functional probe to `NodeTester.ts`.
- Expose a `healthCheck()` or `ping()` method on the component.
- Verify status via the `/health` command in the POG2 shell.

### 5. Clinical Verification ✅
- Run `npm run build` to verify neurological integrity.
- Verify the feedback loop via the `Renderer`.
- Update the `walkthrough.md` with real-world proof of functionality.

---

## 📝 Contributor TODO List

1.  [x] **Neurological Mapping**: Update `NeurologicalMap.ts` for all new nodes.

6.  [x] **Peer Review Sync**: Link clinical research data to `POG2_KNOWLEDGEBASE.md`.
7.  [x] **Metabolic Monitoring**: Add `healthCheck()` methods to all specialized limbs and engines.
8.  [x] **Visual Roadmapping**: Update `ARCHITECTURE.md` diagrams when structural paths change.
9.  [ ] **Pipeline Continuity**: Ensure Cinematic Mode run-continuity (Scene 1 -> 2 -> 3).
10. [x] **Clinical Auditing**: Run `npm run lint` and `ClinicalAuditTool` before every PR.

---

## 🛠️ CLI Reference (Sovereign Commands)

The POG2 CLI uses **Commander** for top-level commands and a **conversational REPL** with slash-commands for deep interaction.

### Top-Level Commands
- `pog2 init`: Initialize or repair Sovereign Context files (`.pog2.md`, `.rules.md`, `.manifest.md`).
- `pog2 process <intent>`: Execute a single task managed by Kimi. (`-y` for auto-proceed).
- `pog2 think <intent>`: Trigger a metabolic reflection cycle (I Ching thinking).
- `pog2 dispatch <capabilityId> <payload>`: Directly invoke an AI capability.
- `pog2 health`: Deep clinical audit (Alias for `system health`). (`--json` for raw data).
- `pog2 personality`: Display AI personality archetypes.
- `pog2 consolidate`: Trigger the Subconscious Memory Processor.
- `pog2 system status`: hierarchical routing diagnostics (`-r` for visual tree).
- `pog2 system audit <target>`: Scan a file or directory for Sovereign Law violations.
- `pog2 system capabilities`: Deep scan for available engines and limbs.
- `pog2 vs open [path]`: Open a Sovereign Workspace in VS Code.
- `pog2 gutenberg ingest <id>`: Download and store a book in the library.
- `pog2 pipeline run <bookId>`: Run a full creative story-to-media pipeline.

### REPL Slash Commands
Invoke these inside the conversational shell:
- `/help`: Show all shortcuts.
- `/status`: Show system mode, workspace, and model cooldowns.
- `/capabilities`: Discover latent substrate engines.
- `/registry`: List all registered substrate tools.
- `/vision`: Trigger spatial observation / eye capture.
- `/shadow`: Consult global architectural maps.
- `/memetics`: Research from browser history kernels.
- `/syntropy`: Harmonize external metadata (.claude/.gemini).
- `/pull [model]`: Directly pull an Ollama model.
- `/vs`: Open current workspace in VS Code.
- `/exit`: Power down the Sovereign Organism.

---

## 🤖 AI Model Standards (DOC Context)

Current anchor models for POG2's Distributed Orchestration Cognition:
- **Reasoning (Master)**: Kimi v2.5 / DeepSeek-R1 (Local Fallback)
- **Execution (Executive)**: Qwen 2.5 Coder (14B)
- **Reflex (Reactive)**: VibeThinker 1.5B (Autopoietic Seed)

*VibeThinker must not be modified by external project scripts.*

---

pog2 status

# GEMINI.md — POG2 Sovereign Command Line Intelligence

## Project Overview

POG2 is a highly sophisticated "Sovereign Command Line Intelligence" system designed with a biological nervous system architecture. It operates as an interactive CLI agent that brings the power of Gemini (and other models) directly into the terminal, specialized for software engineering, reverse engineering (specifically RS3 game cache), and autonomous content generation.

### Core Architecture: DOC (Distributed Orchestration Cognition)

- **Biological Inspiration:** Organized into **Limbs** (executors) and **Engines** (processing centers).
- **Ternary Routing:** Tasks are classified into three tiers (Yang, YinYang, Yin) and routed to appropriate models (Cloud vs. Local).
- **Binary Absolutes:** Enforces strict success/failure states.
- **Sovereign Laws:**
  1. **NO MOCKS:** Real APIs and implementations only.
  2. **NO PLACEHOLDERS:** No TODOs or stubs in generated code.
  3. **TSC TIGHT:** Strict TypeScript compliance.
  4. **CLINICAL LOGGING:** All cognitive states are traceable.

### Key Components

- **OrchestrateEngine:** The "Brain" (Kimi-led) that maps decisions across 65+ registered tools.
- **Limb System:** Categorized into spatial, technical, creative, metaphysical, and sensory domains.
- **rsmv Substrate:** A deep integration for RS3 game cache forensics, decoding, and 3D visualization.
- **Cinematic Pipeline:** Autonomous story-to-media generation (storyboard -> image -> voice -> video).

## Building and Running

### Installation

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm run install-global # To use 'pog2' command globally
```

### Key Commands

- `pog2 process "task"`: Execute a task managed by the Orchestrator.
- `pog2 system status`: Audit the current sovereign state and model routing.
- `pog2 system health`: Deep clinical audit of all neurological nodes.
- `pog2 atlas hud <id>`: Decompile and audit a game interface.
- `pog2 pipeline run <bookId>`: Run the autonomous cinematic generation pipeline.
- `pog2 rsmv --view <modelId>`: View a 3D model from the cache.

### Development Scripts (package.json)

- `npm run build`: Compile TypeScript.
- `npm run dev`: Run CLI in development mode using `tsx`.
- `npm run typecheck`: Strict type checking with `tsc`.
- `npm run lint`: Linting with ESLint.

## Development Conventions

### Coding Standards

- **Strict Typing:** Always use explicit types; avoid `any`.
- **Readonly by Default:** Prefer immutability.
- **Result Type:** Use `Result<T>` for fallible operations to ensure explicit error handling.
- **Clinical Logging:** Use the `pino` logger for all internal states.

### Architectural Rules

- **Domain Isolation:** Follow the domain-scoped tool access defined in `ToolRegistry.ts`.
- **Hexagram Manager:** All high-level decisions must be routed through `HexagramManager.ts` to maintain archetypal integrity.
- **Adversarial Reflection:** Use the `GhostLimb` for auditing results and providing adversarial feedback.

### Testing & Validation

- **No Mocks:** Tests must use real implementations and substrates.
- **Empirical Reproduction:** For bugs, always confirm the failure state empirically before applying a fix.
- **Clinical Audit:** Use `pog2 system audit <path>` to check for Sovereign Law violations.

## Workspace Structure

- `src/cli.ts`: Main entry point and command registrations.
- `src/ToolRegistry.ts`: Central hub for all sovereign tools.
- `src/engines/`: Core logic engines (Orchestrate, Code, Embed, etc.).
- `src/limbs/`: Specialized executors (Spatial, Technical, Creative, etc.).
- `src/rsmv/`: RS3 Cache decoding and rsmv integration.
- `src/core/models.ts`: Fundamental type definitions and archetypes.
- `memory/`: Local VectorDB and pedagogical storage.
